summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official: Learning Day - Sleeve Collection p02 ## Introduction In this session, we will explore the process of creating various types of sleeves using Marvelous Designer. The focus will be on the techniques for constructing lantern sleeves, shoulder sleeves, and pleated sleeves, as well as sewing details and adjustments for fabric behavior. ## Lantern Sleeve Creation When making a lantern sleeve, we need to lengthen the sleeve to ensure it has enough fabric for the folds to pile up. 1. **Select the Outer Line**: Start by selecting the outer line of the sleeve bottom and set the inner line of the lining. 2. **Cut the Seam Allowance**: After cutting the seam allowance, you will have the sleeve opening. 3. **Align the Lines**: Select the top and bottom two straight lines to align them properly. 4. **Shrink the Sleeve Opening**: This will help the folds to pile up effectively. 5. **Seam Allowance**: Use 100% of the seam allowance on the sleeve opening. 6. **Maintain Original Length**: Keep the length of the original line to avoid stretching. Next, utilize the **Plus Point Division Tool** to add a center point in the sleeve. Click on the line to set the length and proportion in the fold window. The **Extension Tool** can be used to create a more flexible sheet by extending the sheet from the middle to both sides. ## Shoulder Sleeve Construction To create a shoulder sleeve: 1. **Create a Long Strip**: Click on the 3D strip. 2. **Determine Position**: In the 2D window, position it according to the blue position point. 3. **Draw Inner Line**: After confirming the position, draw the inner line and align it with the outer line of the strip. 4. **Cut and Sew**: Cut and sew this to create a long strip of the shoulder. 5. **Freeze the Strip**: This avoids instability during future modifications. 6. **Extend the Sleeve Strip**: Use the extension tool to extend the strip of the sleeve part for more fabric and folds. Adjust the curve after extending to ensure smoothness. ## Making Non-Sew Strips When creating non-sew sleeves: 1. **Delete Original Board**: Create a long strip board using the rectangular tool. 2. **Set Width**: Enter the width of the board in the spring window. 3. **Sew the Long Strip**: Attach it to the hemline. 4. **Adjust Shape**: Shorten the height of the two sides of the board to adjust its shape. 5. **Apply 100% Elasticity**: This prevents stretching by the sleeve board. ## Embroidery and Folds When making hulu embroidery: 1. **Create Vertical Internal Lines**: Create a few vertical internal lines according to the curve line and sew them into board slices. 2. **Separate Lines**: Align the internal lines to the board slices. 3. **Adjust Bottom Lines**: Move them left and right to widen the board slices. For smoother curves, use the **Adjustment Point Tool** and apply elasticity to the outer line of the board to create the desired draw effect. ## Double-Fold and Cut Sleeves The first fold-and-cut sleeve production method resembles the white-shoulder group: 1. **Make Sleeves Longer**: Set an inner line and cut it into a seam. 2. **Align Inner Line**: Align with the outer line of the board and add points. 3. **Sew the Board**: After simulating and hardening, sew the board to enhance the folding effect. The second method involves creating pleated sleeves: 1. **Draw Internal Pattern**: Set the internal line according to the desired number of pleats. 2. **Cut and Delete**: Align the bottom line with the left line, cut, and sew. 3. **Adjust the Pattern**: Use the fold-over tool to create the needed folds. ## Sewing and Layering Techniques When sewing layers: 1. **Sew from the Center**: This helps to avoid crossing the sewing line. 2. **Select All Sewing Lines**: Modify the type of sewing line to 'Turned' for overlapping plackets. While aligning the front and back sides of the fabric, ensure that the sewing width and lengths are consistent to prevent stretching. ## Conclusion This session covered various techniques for creating and adjusting sleeves in Marvelous Designer. From lantern sleeves to complex pleated designs, understanding these methods allows for greater creativity and precision in garment design. ```
